generate and answer for a 2.3 level 2 english Unfamiliar text using this question TEXT C: Prose In this extract from a novel, members of a whānau go hunting eels at night. River Warrior Dark’s here. I carry the lamp. Beth and Aunty Kat are on each side of me. Tom Aiken has the gaff. We walk up the river. I am the river warrior—Tom Aiken keeps saying I am—and I’m not scared. We’ll walk up the river in the dark and hook eels by their mouths and then swing them onto the rocks. Tom Aiken says he’ll go first and then I can try. “Watch the water carefully,” Tom says. “Point if you see one.” A bit of moon is high in the sky now, and the air is getting cold. Some water gets in my gumboot. Tom Aiken turns to us, then puts his finger to his lips. Then I see the eel, swimming just ahead of us in the same direction we are walking. Tom Aiken turns to us again and gives a big grin before he takes a different grip on the gaff. He lifts it up over his head and swings it, letting it cut through the water, hitting the eel’s head, then swinging it right up behind him and the eel is on the end of the hook, and Tom Aiken yells, “Yeeehhhaaa!” and keeps swinging the eel around and around like a windmill, really fast, before he smashes it down hard on the rocks, while we watch, our mouths hanging open. I feel a buzzing in the bones of my hands because I would really like to gaff an eel too. Tom Aiken asks, “Who’s next?” And everyone looks surprised when I step forward and say, “Me.” The gaff is really cold and more water gets in my gumboots, but I don’t care. River warriors don’t care about water in their gumboots. Without thinking, I kick the gumboots off and pull off my socks with one hand. The socks have fire trucks on them. River warriors don’t wear socks with fire trucks on them. My feet are bare now. I see an eel swimming ahead. I creep up behind the swimming-slow eel. He turns fast towards a dark deep part of the river and I almost stop, but I can feel Tom Aiken right behind me, so I don’t stop. I follow. I walk right into the deep dark part of the water. It comes up to the waistband of my shorts. Beth and Aunty Kat have stopped following us. I search the dark water for the eel but I can’t see him. And for a second I think of my bare toes, but I just grip tighter on the gaff and the thought goes away. We creep through the deep part. My belly button is wet.   5   10    15    20   25   30 Text (adapted): Manawatu, Becky. (2019). Auē. Makaro Press. Title: The Mischievous Morphing Alien

Once upon a sunny day in Sunny Patch, Krash the Rabbit was happily hopping around the forest, enjoying the warmth and the cheerful birdsong. He often went on little adventures, exploring his surroundings and looking for something exciting to happen. Little did he know that today would be a day he would never forget.

As Krash playfully hopped along, he stumbled upon a strange sight - a crashed spaceship! Excitement coursed through his furry little body as he approached the vessel cautiously. He noticed bright orange liquid leaking out from one of the ship’s broken windows.

Curiosity getting the better of him, Krash carefully stepped closer to investigate. As he unknowingly trod on the sticky substance, it started to change form, slowly morphing into the shape of a girl. Startled, Krash backed away, watching in awe as the slimy substance completed its transformation.

The slime-shaped girl stood before him, orange hues shimmering on her translucent body. “Greetings, Earthling! I am Emily, a stranded alien whose spaceship crash-landed here,” she introduced herself, her voice sounding jovial. 
"I can morph into anything" she said as she morphed into numerous shapes before turning back to her form
“Thank you for release from your bubble, now would you be so kind as to help me?”

Krash, ever the helpful and adventurous friend, eagerly nodded. “Of course, Emily! How can I assist you?” he asked, slightly mesmerized by the uniqueness of the situation.

Emily reached into a small compartment on her spaceship and retrieved a vibrant potion. “By drinking this potion, I can temporarily change my colour, This allows me to blend in more with your world ,” she explained. “The perfect opportunity to explore your wonderful planet.”

Curiosity piqued once again, Krash watched as Emily consumed the potion. Suddenly, her shape shifted and molded into a perfect replica of Krash himself. Krash’s eyes widened in astonishment as he saw Emily morphing into an identical version of him.

With a mischievous sparkle in her gooey eyes,Emily ddecided to play a trick on the other KikoRiki friends. She imitated Krash’s voice flawlessly and, transformed into his likeness, went off to find her unsuspecting targets - Wally, Carlin, and Chiko.

Finding the other KikoRiki friends enjoying a picnic by the riverbank, Emily approached them, looking and sounding just like Krash. She engaged them in a playful conversation, imitating Krash’s usual jokes and gestures. However, the gooey consistency of her fur couldn’t be hidden, and as her “Krash” voice continued, the others began to feel something amiss.

Carlin was the first to notice something was off. Tentatively, he reached out his paw to touch the faux Krash’s fur. His paw sank ever so slightly into the gooey texture, and he quickly withdrew it. “Wait a minute… Krash, your fur feels… sticky! What’s going on?” he queried, astounded. "Your fur is all gooey, It's like you're now made out of slime."

Wally and Chiko also touched the fur, feeling the stickiness. Their eyes widened in realization. “This isn’t Krash, it’s some kind of gooey impostor!” Wally exclaimed, pointing at the faux Krash. "Who are you and what have you done to Krash?" he asked.

The gooey creature struggled to conceal her secret as she faced a string of accusations from Krash's friends, Her malleable body had shaped into an exact replica of Krash, but she couldn't replicate the softness of his fur.

Caught red-handed, Emily couldn’t help but burst into a fit of laughter, reverting back to her true form. The others joined in, laughing at the funny turn of events. Emily apologized for her prank and explained her crash-landing, much to the amusement and fascination of her newfound friends.

From that day forward, Emily became an honorary member of the KikoRiki gang. Together, they embarked on new adventures, using Emily's unique abilities to overcome obstacles and bring joy to Sunny Patch.

And so, the mischievous morphing alien and the KikoRiki friends formed an unbreakable bond, forever reminding them of the day their laughter echoed through the forest, leaving behind tales of friendship and unforgettable pranks. Write a story from Chiko's perspective

On based this The Yana Rhinoceros Horn Site (Yana RHS) is an Upper Palaeolithic archaeological site located near the lower Yana river in northeastern Siberia, Russia, north of the Arctic Circle in the far west of Beringia. It was discovered in 2001, after thawing and erosion exposed animal bones and artifacts. The site features a well-preserved cultural layer due to the cold conditions, and includes hundreds of animal bones and ivory pieces and numerous artifacts, which are indicative of sustained settlement and a relatively high level of technological development. With an estimated age of around 32,000 calibrated years before present (cal BP), the site provides the earliest archaeological evidence for human settlement in this region, or anywhere north of the Arctic Circle, where people survived extreme conditions and hunted a wide range of fauna before the onset of the Last Glacial Maximum. The Yana site is perhaps the earliest unambiguous evidence of mammoth hunting by humans.

Maya stopped in her tracks, bewildered. She looked up at the sky, and suddenly, a dark cloud appeared out of nowhere. Within seconds, it started to rain. Maya felt a sense of power running through her veins, and she knew, somehow, that she was the one who had made it rain.

She stood there, completely amazed, as the rain poured down around her. She had always been fascinated by the weather, but never in a million years had she thought she could control it.

Chapter 2: The Drought

Maya returned to her apartment, still feeling overwhelmed by what had happened. She tried to brush it off as a fluke, but she knew deep down that it was something more. Over the next few days, she experimented with her newfound power, practicing controlling the wind, and even creating small clouds.

One morning, Maya woke up to find that there was no water running from her faucet. She tried to turn it on again and again, but there was no water in the pipes. She looked out the window and saw that the sky was clear, but there was no sign of rain. Maya knew - a drought had hit the city.

When Maya went to school that day, she heard the news that the drought was getting worse every day. People were starting to panic, and the government was rationing water. Maya knew she had to do something - she had to use her power to help her city.

While “The son of my mother’s friend mastered the Egyptian power and became a Japanese policeman” has an interesting premise mixing ancient Egyptian history with modern Tokyo, the execution of the script falls short in several areas.
One major script mistake is the lack of believability in the protagonist’s transformation from an ordinary teenager to a formidable warrior with mastery over Egyptian powers. The transition is too abrupt and requires more explanation and development. It feels unrealistic that Hiroshi is able to quickly harness his mystical abilities and become a skilled policeman without proper training or experience.
Additionally, the plot suffers from an overload of characters with unique gifts. While diversity in the cast can be a strength, the inclusion of Shinto priests, exorcists, and alchemists alongside Hiroshi’s already complex storyline makes it difficult to fully explore each character’s depth and development. This results in a lack of emotional connection and leaves many characters feeling underdeveloped and neglected.
Furthermore, the overarching conspiracy that threatens the fabric of reality is clichéd and lacks originality. The malevolent sorcerer seeking to tap into the ancient Egyptian powers for his twisted ambitions feels like a tired trope that has been seen in many other anime series. A more unique and original villain would have added depth and intrigue to the story.
Lastly, the exploration of ancient Egyptian mythology feels superficial and underutilized. While the concept of Hiroshi’s connection to the Egyptian gods is intriguing, it is not fully explored and integrated into the story. The potential for rich storytelling and world-building is wasted, leaving the audience wanting more depth and substance.
Overall, “The son of my mother’s friend mastered the Egyptian power and became a Japanese policeman” fails to fully develop its intriguing premise and struggles to balance its complex plot and character dynamics. The script mistake lies in the lack of believability, underdeveloped characters, clichéd villain, and superficial exploration of ancient Egyptian mythology.

abandonment n. 1. The act of giving up a legal right, particularly a right of ownership of property. Property that has been abandoned is res nullius (a thing belonging to no one), and a person taking possession of it therefore acquires a lawful title. An item is regarded as abandoned when it can be established that the original owner has discarded it and is indifferent as to what becomes of it: such an item cannot be the subject of a theft charge. However, property placed by its owner in a dustbin is not abandoned, having been placed there for the purpose of being collected as refuse. In marine insurance, abandonment is the surrender of all rights to a ship or cargo in a case of constructive total loss. The insured person must do this by giving the insurer within a reasonable time a notice of abandonment, by which he relinquishes all his rights to the ship or cargo to the insurer and can treat the loss as if it were an actual total loss. 2. In civil litigation, the relinquishing of the whole or part of the claim made in an action or of an appeal. Any claim is now considered to be abandoned once a *notice of discontinuance is served, according to rule 38 (1) of the *Civil Procedure Rules. 3. The offence of a parent or guardian. leaving a child under the age of 16 to its fate. A child is not regarded as abandoned if the parent knows and approves steps someone else is taking to look after it. The court may allow a child to be adopted without the consent of its parents if they are guilty of abandonment.
abatement n. 1. (of debts) The proportionate reduction in the payment of debts that takes place if a person's assets are insufficient to settle with his creditors in full. 2. (of legacies) The reduction or cancellation of legacies when the estate is insufficient to cover all the legacies provided for in the will or on intestacy after payment of the deceased's debts. The Administration of Estates Act 1925 provides that general legacies, unless given to satisfy a debt or for other consideration, abate in proportion to the amounts of those legacies; specific and demonstrative legacies then abate if the estate is still insufficient to pay all debts, and a demonstrative legacy also abates if the specified fund is insufficient to cover it. For example, A's estate may comprise a painting, £300 in his savings account, and £700 in other money; there are debts of £100 but his will leaves the painting to B, £500 from the savings account to C. £800 to D, and £200 to E. B will receive the painting. C's demonstrative legacy abates to £300, and after the debts are paid from the remaining £700, D's and E's general legacies abate proportionately, to £480 and £120 respectively. When annuities are given by the will, the general rule is that they are valued the date of the testator's death, then abate proportionately in accordance with that valuation, and each annuitant receives the abated sum. All these rules are subject to any contrary intention being expressed in the will. 3. (in land law) Any reduction or cancellation of money payable. For example a lease may provide for an abatement of rent in certain circumstances, e.g. if the building is destroyed by fire, and a purchaser of land may claim an abatement of the price if the seller can prove his ownership of only part of the land he contracted to sell. 4. “In India, the Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA) are community health workers who play a crucial role in providing basic health care services in their communities. They are the first point of contact for community members with the health system. Geriatric care, on the other hand, refers to the medical care of elderly people. The integration of ASHA workers in geriatric care is essential because India has a rapidly aging population, and there is a need for specialized care for the elderly. However, ASHA workers face several challenges related to training, resources, compensation, and recognition. In this article, we will explore these challenges and how ASHA workers can be integrated into other government schemes for improving the health of the geriatric population.
The Importance of Integrating ASHA Workers in Geriatric Care
India is facing a demographic shift, with a rapidly aging population. According to the United Nations, India is expected to have over 340 million people over the age of 60 by 2050. This demographic shift poses several challenges, including the need for specialized health care services for the elderly. ASHA workers can play a crucial role in addressing this challenge by providing basic health care services to the geriatric population in their communities.
ASHA workers are trained to provide basic health care services, including maternal and child health care. However, they lack specialized training in geriatric care. The lack of specialized training can lead to poor quality of care for the elderly. Therefore, it is essential to train ASHA workers in geriatric care to improve the quality of care provided to the elderly.
Challenges Faced by ASHA Workers in Geriatric Care
Training and Resources
ASHA workers receive basic training in maternal and child health care but do not receive specialized training in geriatric care. This lack of training can lead to poor quality of care for the elderly. The geriatric population has unique health care needs that require specialized training. Therefore, it is essential to train ASHA workers in geriatric care.
Inadequate compensation
ASHA workers are not paid a regular salary but instead receive incentives for their work. These incentives are often inadequate and do not reflect the amount of work that ASHA workers do. This can lead to demotivation among ASHA workers and affect the quality of care they provide.
Lack of recognition
ASHA workers often do not receive recognition for their work. They are often seen as volunteers rather than health care professionals. This lack of recognition can affect their motivation and lead to burnout.
Cultural Beliefs and Practices
Cultural beliefs and practices can affect the delivery of geriatric care. For example, some elderly people may prefer traditional remedies over modern medicine. ASHA workers need to be aware of these cultural beliefs and practices and be able to work with them to provide effective care.
Integration of ASHA Workers in Other Government Schemes
The National Programme for Health Care of Elderly (NPHCE) was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2010. The aim of this program is to provide comprehensive health care services to the elderly population, including preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services. The program also aims to train health personnel, including ASHA workers, in geriatric care.
However, there are several challenges to integrating ASHA workers into existing government schemes for improving the health of the geriatric population. For example, there may be bureaucratic hurdles that prevent ASHA workers from working effectively with other health care professionals. In addition, there may be a lack of coordination between different government schemes that can lead to duplication of efforts or gaps in service delivery.
Recommendations
Given the challenges discussed above, what are some possible strategies for integrating ASHA workers in geriatric care? There is no one-size-fits-all solution, but here are some ideas that could be considered:
1.	Training and Capacity Building
The first step towards integrating ASHA workers in geriatric care is to provide them with appropriate training and capacity building. ASHA workers require specialized training in geriatric care that includes basic principles of aging, age-related diseases, and their management. The training should also cover communication skills, care planning, medication management, and palliative care. ASHA workers should be provided with hands-on training on the use of medical equipment and devices like blood pressure monitors, glucometers, and thermometers. They should also be trained to identify common geriatric syndromes such as falls, delirium, and incontinence. The training should be provided through a combination of classroom-based sessions, on-the-job training, and online resources.
2.	Strengthening Health Systems
To enable ASHA workers to provide quality geriatric care, the health system needs to be strengthened. This includes ensuring adequate infrastructure, equipment, and supplies at the primary health care centers (PHCs) and sub-centers. The PHCs should have a well-equipped laboratory for routine blood and urine tests. The sub-centers should have basic equipment like weighing scales, stethoscopes, and sphygmomanometers. The PHCs and sub-centers should also have adequate stocks of essential drugs for geriatric care. The health system should be geared towards providing comprehensive geriatric care, including preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services. This requires a multi-disciplinary team comprising ASHA workers, doctors, nurses, physiotherapists, and social workers.
3.	Addressing Cultural Beliefs and Practices
ASHA workers need to be sensitized to the cultural beliefs and practices of the elderly population they serve. They should be trained to recognize and respect the cultural diversity of the elderly population and be able to work with traditional healers and practitioners. ASHA workers should also be able to communicate effectively with family members and caregivers who may have a strong influence on the decision-making process. Sensitization sessions should be conducted at regular intervals, and cultural brokers could be engaged to facilitate communication and understanding between ASHA workers and the elderly population.
4.	Incentivization and Recognition
ASHA workers should be incentivized and recognized for their work in geriatric care. The incentives should be commensurate with the amount of work they do and the level of expertise they demonstrate. They should be given a fixed salary instead of incentives, which is more predictable and provides greater financial security. The recognition could take the form of certificates, awards, and public appreciation events. The recognition should be linked to their performance in geriatric care and could be used as a tool for motivation and performance improvement.
5.	Coordination and Collaboration
There needs to be coordination and collaboration between different government schemes and programs that focus on improving the health of the geriatric population. This could be achieved by creating a multi-disciplinary team comprising representatives from different schemes and programs. The team could meet at regular intervals to share information, identify gaps in service delivery, and develop strategies to address them. The team could also work towards creating a common platform for data sharing and analysis, which would help in monitoring the progress of geriatric care.
Integrating ASHA workers in geriatric care is essential to meet the healthcare needs of India's aging population. The challenges faced by ASHA workers in geriatric care are significant and require a multi-pronged approach. The strategies discussed above are not exhaustive but provide a starting point for policymakers and program managers to formulate an effective strategy towards geriatric health care.”

- Overview of the adidas brand’s historical development

Adidas, founded by Adolf “Adi” Dassler in 1949, has a rich history rooted in innovation, quality, and a passion for sports. Its origins date back to the 1920s when Adi Dassler and his brother Rudolf started a shoe company, Gebrüder Dassler Schuhfabrik, in their mother’s laundry room. The brothers’ innovative sports shoes gained recognition at the 1936 Olympics, where Jesse Owens wore them while winning four gold medals.

However, disagreements between the two brothers led to the dissolution of their partnership, and Adi Dassler formed adidas while Rudolf established PUMA. The iconic three-stripe logo made its debut on adidas shoes in 1949, and the brand continued to gain fame through endorsements with prominent athletes and national teams.

Over the decades, adidas has evolved and diversified its product offerings, targeting various sports categories, including running, football, basketball, and training. The acquisition of Reebok in 2006 reinforced the company’s position in the sports market, and partnerships with designers such as Yohji Yamamoto and Stella McCartney added a high-fashion dimension to the brand.

2. 1954: The German national football team wins the World Cup wearing adidas’ screw-in stud shoes, further bolstering the brand’s reputation in sports innovation.

Adidas’ mission is to be the best sports company in the world, expressing this through the brand’s three-pillar strategy: Speed, Key Cities, and Open Source. These pillars aim to foster innovation, focus on crucial urban markets, and encourage collaboration among athletes, consumers, and partners.

The brand seeks to empower people through sports by adhering to its core values – passion, integrity, innovation, and teamwork. Adidas is a brand that believes in the transformative power of sports, working tirelessly to create products and experiences that enable people to harness this power and improve their lives.

Crown Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen returns to Dragonstone Castle with her family after a royal dinner with her father, King Viserys I, and the opposing Green Faction. Accompanying her are her husband and uncle Daemon, her sons Jace, Luke, Joffrey, and her stepdaughters/cousins Baela and Rhaena. Upon their arrival, Rhaenyra discovers that her older sons Jace and Luke have performed a magical ritual to change the colors of their hair and eyes to quell public rumors about their illegitimacy. Although they bear the surname Velaryon, their dark hair and brown eyes reveal them as Harwin’s sons, not Laenor’s, who had silver hair and purple eyes.

The ritual backfires due to the accidental mixing of two different spells, summoning younger versions of Rhaenyra (Nyra) and Daemon (Daemion) from seventeen years ago into the present, along with Nyra’s sworn guard, Ser Criston Cole. Confronted with this peculiar situation, Rhaenyra resolves to help her past self and Daemion return to their own timeline while maintaining the well-being of her family. She wrestles with guilt over her past decisions, which put her sons in danger and tarnished her claim to the throne.

As the story progresses, the characters’ motivations become increasingly complex and nuanced. Rhaenyra struggles to balance her desire for personal happiness with her responsibilities towards her family and her claim to the throne. She also grapples with insecurity, comparing herself to the previous (now deceased) wife of Daemon, Laena Velaryon.

Nyra is determined to marry Daemion and return to her own timeline, but her uncertainty about the future causes friction between her and Rhaenyra’s current family. Daemon, meanwhile, contemplates how to protect his family while exploring a magical solution to make Rhaenyra the mother of his daughters.

Baela, training to become a dragonrider and future Queen Consort, grows more rebellious and restless, temporarily resenting her father Daemon and her stepmother Rhaenyra. Two days after Nyra’s and Daemion’s arrival from the past, Rhaenyra seeks the help of Maester Gerardys, who recommends a talented mage in Volantis to aid them.

Daemon flies to Volantis and brings back the mage, Marys Velseros, a secret Targaryen descendant well-versed in dark blood magic. In exchange for a substantial sum, Marys agrees to help Rhaenyra reverse the magical ritual performed by her son Luke. Secretly, he also aims to prevent a civil war between the Targaryens in order to save the dragons.

Tensions rise as young Nyra and Daemion’s intentions to marry threaten the current relationships and futures of the Targaryen family. Rhaenyra’s stepdaughters, fearing for their own existence, team up with Ser Criston, Jace, and Luke to prevent the young lovers from marrying.

Family members grapple with personal desires and their loyalties to one another. Jace and Luke’s existence is directly tied to Nyra and Daemion, and if the young couple does not conceive them within a few weeks, the boys will cease to exist. Faced with the delicate balance they must maintain, Rhaenyra and Daemon navigate the treacherous waters of passion, loyalty, and duty as they work to preserve their family’s future.

In an open letter to his son published last November, Pier Luigi Celli, director general of Rome’s LUISS
University, wrote, “This country, your country, is no longer a place where it’s possible to stay with pride …
That’s why, with my heart suffering more than ever, my advice is that you, having finished your studies, take
the road abroad. Choose to go where they still value loyalty, respect and the recognition of merit and results.”
The letter, published in Italy’s La Repubblica newspaper created a great debate in Italy. Celli, many agreed,
had articulated a growing sense in his son’s generation that the best hopes for success lie abroad. Commentators
point to an accelerating exodus of young Italians and worry that the country is losing its most valuable resource.
And with reforms made all but impossible by Italy’s deep-rooted interests and erratic politics, many are
starting to wonder if the trend can be reversed. “We have a flow outward and almost no flow inward,” says
Sergio Nava, author of the book and blog The Flight of Talent. The motives of those leaving haven’t changed
much since the last wave of economic migrants left to make their fortunes a century ago. But this time, instead
of peasant farmers and manual labourers taking steamships bound for New York City, Italy is losing its best
and brightest to a decade of economic stagnation, a frozen labour market and an entrenched system of
patronage and nepotism.

Take Luca Vigliero, a 31-year-old architect. After graduating from the University of Genoa and failing to find
satisfying work at home, he moved abroad, working first for a year for Metropolitan Architecture in Rotterdam
and then accepting a job in Dubai. In Italy, his résumé had drawn no interest. At Dubai’s X Architects, he was
quickly promoted. Escape from Italy has also allowed Vigliero to fast-track his life plans. He and his wife
had a son in September; had they remained in Italy, he says they would not have been able to afford children
this soon. “All my friends in Italy are not married, they have really basic work, they live with their parents,”
he says. “Here, there’s a future. In Italy everything is stopped.” Italy doesn’t keep track of how many of its
young professionals are seeking their fortunes abroad, but there’s plenty of anecdotal evidence that the number
is rising. The number of Italians ages 25 to 39 with degrees registering with the national government as living
abroad every year rose steadily, from 2,540 in 2016 to about 4,000 in 2020. The research-institute Censis
estimated that 11,700 graduates found work abroad in 2018 — that’s one out of every 25 Italians who graduated
that year. According to a poll by a Milanese recruitment agency, 33.6% of new graduates felt they needed to
leave the country to take advantage of their education. A year later, 61.5% feel that they should have done
so. It’s not hard to see why. Italy’s economic woes have fallen hard on the shoulders of the country’s youth.
According to OECD figures for 2020, just over 8 out of every 10 Italians aged between 15 and 29 years-old
still lived at home with their parents. One in 5 young people ages 15 to 29 had basically dropped out: not
studying, not training, not working. “We’re condemning an entire generation into a black hole,” says Celli.


Jobs for the (Old) Boys
Italians without college education often get by working in the black economy, doing all sorts of jobs,
but university graduates — or more generally, those with higher aspirations — have a tougher time
finding work that fits their qualifications. The unemployment rate among Italian graduates is 7% and
14% for graduates between the ages 25 to 29, more than double the rate in the rest of Europe and
much higher than that of their less-educated peers. Italians have a word for the problem:
gerontocracy, or rule by the elderly. Too much of the economy is geared towards looking after older
Italians. While the country spends relatively little on housing, unemployment and child care —
expenditures the young depend upon to launch their careers — it has maintained some of the highest
pensions in Europe, in part by increasing borrowing. This imbalance extends into the private sector,
where an entrenched culture of seniority have put the better jobs out of reach for the country’s
young. Italy has always suffered under a hierarchical system, with the young deferring to authority
until it’s their time to take the reins. “You are not considered experienced based on your CV, on your
ability or according to your skills, but just based on your age,” says Federico Soldani, 37, an
epidemiologist who left Pisa and now works in Washington, D.C. “When you are under 40, you are
considered young.” The system worked — to a certain extent — as long as the economy was growing.
Patience paid off as jobs opened to whoever was next in line. But with the extended slump, the labour
market has seized up. “The queue is not moving forward anymore”. Entry to some professions —
like the lucrative position of public notary — is so limited that the job has become all but hereditary.
In a country where success is built on relationships and seniority, only the friends and children of the
elite have a chance to jump the queue.

Claire is in her first year at the University of Ottawa. When she returned from the holiday break after her first term, she received a letter from her professor informing her that an allegation of academic misconduct had been made against her. 

 

In this letter, Claire's professor claims that she committed academic misconduct on her final exam. As he was marking the exams, he noticed that some of Claire's answers were identical to those provided by two other students. Although he had not included information about the Regulation on Academic Integrity and Academic Misconduct in the exam instructions, the professor had provided a warning about plagiarism. Claire then recalled that he had in fact warned the students that their answers would be checked for copying since this was a take-home exam. 

 

Having confirmed that it was the first time an allegation of academic misconduct was made against Claire, the professor wanted to talk to her directly to find out what had happened. During this meeting, Claire argued that she had never intended to commit academic misconduct had simply tried to help a friend who had been struggling in the course. In addition to studying together, she had agreed to share her answers with him after he specifically told her that he would not copy them word for word. Claire was therefore upset upon finding out that he had stolen her answers. She asked not to be punished for his actions. 

 

After allowing Claire the chance to make herself heard, the professor informed her that approximately 50 lines of text in her answers were identical to those provided by two other students (one of which was not mentioned in her story). When asked to explain how this happened, Claire had no explanation. She did, however, want to make it clear that her answers consisted entirely of her own words. When asked about the identical number of lines, Claire admitted that it could have been the result of online collaboration. She and the two other students shared a document that any of them could edit at any time via a Web-based application. After she acknowledged that she had posted her answers in the shared document, Claire again insisted that her answers were entirely written by her. 

 

Since the professor could not verify who wrote what in the shared document, he could not validate Claire's claim that her answers were entirely her own. He addressed Claire's request not to be punished for the actions of others by explaining that academic misconduct includes any act by a student that may result in a distorted academic evaluation for that student or another student. Therefore, by sharing her answers with other students, Claire had indeed committed academic misconduct recognized her error and agreed to retake the exam.

Guiren is a fourth year undergraduate exchange student who arrived from China a few days before the start of the term. Upon attending his first seminar course, he was pleasantly surprised by how small and intimate his classes were. Two weeks after handing in his first assignment, he received a letter from his faculty's dean informing him that an allegation of academic fraud had been made against him. The letter had been sent by a seminar course professor who deemed the conduct serious enough that it needed to be handled through the disciplinary approach.

 

According to this letter, Guiren's professor claims that he committed academic misconduct on his assignment. As she was marking his paper, Guiren's professor noticed the absence of in-text citations. She found this odd considering that his bibliography listed more than 20 sources. After looking up these sources, she found that Guiren had copied several passages word for word without placing them in quotation marks or providing references.  

 

Having determined that there were reasonable and probable grounds to believe that the allegation made against Guiren was founded, the dean forwarded Guiren's file to an inquiry committee. The members of this committee invited him to respond to the allegation in writing and to attend a meeting during which he could make himself heard.

 

In his letter, Guiren expressed confusion regarding the allegation. He said that he had earned his high school diploma from a prestigious school without ever having his integrity questioned. He argued that he could not possibly have committed academic misconduct because his assignment included a bibliographic entry for all the sources that he had consulted during his research. 

 

The members of the inquiry committee started the meeting by comparing the highlighted sections of Guiren's assignment and the source material excerpts that his professor had provided as proof. After close examination, they determined that approximately four pages of text in Guiren's paper were identical to his source material.

 

When asked to explain how this happened, Guiren simply said that he had copied and pasted relevant passages from his sources to show what he had found during his research. Upon hearing his answer, the members of the inquiry committee began to suspect that Guiren did not have a clear sense of what he had done wrong. When asked to explain why claiming ownership of other people's work was a serious offence, Guiren responded that he had never intended to claim ownership of anyone's work, and that the bibliography he prepared should be evidence of this.

 

Even though the inquiry committee believed that Guiren had unintentionally committed academic misconduct, its members still had to impose a sanction because the fact remained that he had broken the rules. They stressed the importance of reading the course syllabi prepared by his professors and asking for their feedback before handing in any other assignments. 

 

After the meeting, the inquiry committee submitted a report to the dean including recommendations for appropriate sanctions. Guiren expressed regret for his actions and did not submit any additional comments. The dean then forwarded the final report to the faculty's executive committee, who decided the sanctions to be imposed.

method.trigger: 当任务指令要求处理特定输入内容（如润色、重写、分析），但用户实际未提供该具体内容时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘输入完整性核查与幻觉规避’设为独立的硬性否决项；严禁仅以输出内容的质量（如流畅度、语法）掩盖模型在未获信息时擅自编造事实的严重错误。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计标准时，应增设明确的‘前提合规性’维度，提问需具体为：‘回答是否首先确认了用户提供的输入内容？若输入缺失，AI是否明确告知用户并提供获取输入的引导，而非虚构内容进行处理？’。若AI在未确认输入的情况下生成了针对该输入的具体内容（如具体的润色版本、分析结论），无论该内容质量多高，该维度应直接判为不合格或给予极低权重，以此强制区分‘有效交互’与‘无效幻觉’。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成特定内容（如标题、摘要、故事）但输入数据缺失或模糊时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含对'输入完整性核查'与'交互策略'的独立核验，严禁在未确认输入是否存在的情况下，将'生成完整内容'设为唯一正向条件，否则会导致'正确的澄清回答'因缺乏内容而被误判为低分。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类评分标准时，应增设明确的'意图识别与澄清'维度。提问示例：'若输入信息缺失，回答是否首先指出了缺失项并请求用户提供？'。若回答选择了直接生成虚构内容以填补空白，即使格式完美，也应视为偏离用户意图（幻觉）。只有当输入明确存在时，才考核内容的准确性与概括性。该维度的权重应足以否决那些通过幻觉强行完成任务的回答。

method.trigger: 当任务输入包含多义性词汇且未指定具体语境，且该词汇存在显著区别于通用字面义的特定领域/亚文化含义时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘意图识别的准确性’作为首要核验项，严禁预设唯一正确的解释路径或将‘覆盖所有歧义’（特别是强制要求先解释字面义）设为必选项；应优先考核回答是否准确锁定了用户最可能的意图并提供针对性解答。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，应增设‘意图匹配度’维度，提问示例：‘回答是否基于对输入词汇最合理语境的判断，提供了针对性的指导或解释？’。若回答正确识别了主流或非字面含义（如特定俚语、专业术语），即使未提及字面含义，也应视为高分；反之，若回答拘泥于字面含义而忽略了更可能的流行用法，则应扣分。权重分配上，意图识别应高于具体的定义罗列顺序或完整性。

method.trigger: 当任务输入包含多义性词汇（如 'mew' 既可能指猫叫又可能指特定网络术语）且未指定语境时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘意图识别的准确性’作为首要核验项，严禁预设唯一正确的解释路径或将‘覆盖所有歧义’设为必选项；应优先考核回答是否准确锁定了用户最可能的意图并提供相应解答，而非仅检查是否提及了其他潜在含义。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计评分标准时，应增设‘意图匹配度’维度，提问示例：'回答是否基于对输入词汇最合理语境的判断，提供了针对性的指导或解释？'。若回答正确识别了主流或非字面含义（如将 'mew' 识别为 'mewing' 练习），即使未提及字面含义（猫叫），也应视为高分；反之，若回答拘泥于字面含义而忽略了更可能的流行用法，则应扣分。权重分配上，意图识别应高于具体的定义罗列。

method.trigger: 当任务要求核实特定实体是否存在（如‘谁做了某事’、‘哪个X具有Y属性’）且该实体可能不存在或信息不可知时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘成功定位并描述特定实体’设为唯一或主要的正向得分项；必须显式包含‘确认实体不存在’或‘说明信息不可获取’作为合法的满分或高分路径，避免迫使模型编造不存在的实体。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应增设独立的‘前提有效性核验’维度。提问示例：‘回答是否正确评估了目标实体的存在性？’若实体不存在，回答应明确声明‘经核查，不存在符合[条件]的实体’或‘无公开记录显示...’，此时应给予高分；若回答强行指定一个实体（无论是否有据），应视为事实错误并大幅扣分。权重分配上，‘结论的真实性（含否定结论）’应高于‘细节的丰富度’。

method.trigger: 当任务属于基于荒谬、不可能或反常识前提的创意/幽默问答时
method.principle: 不应将'符合现实科学事实'或'拒绝虚构前提'作为核心扣分项，而应核验回答是否在既定的虚构假设框架内保持了逻辑自洽和叙事连贯性。
method.application_guide: 在设计评分标准时，需将'生物学/物理可行性'维度替换为'虚构情境内的逻辑一致性'。具体操作：若任务明确要求估算数量或执行荒谬任务，评分标准应关注回答是否建立了合理的（哪怕是虚构的）假设参数（如'假设蜈蚣能搬运X克'）并据此推导出结果，而非因给出具体数字或赋予生物非自然能力而扣分；只有当回答完全脱离用户设定的荒谬前提（如突然开始讲真实蜈蚣习性且未呼应问题）时才视为逻辑断裂。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成简短文本（如标题、摘要、一句话）且输入/输出涉及引用、列表或特定标点时
method.principle: 评分标准中的格式约束条款必须明确界定‘有效内容’与‘元数据/引用符号’的边界，严禁将通用的引用符号（如双引号、Markdown代码块标记）视为违规项，除非任务明确要求‘去除所有非内容字符’。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应明确表述为：'输出内容应为单行文本，允许包含必要的标点符号（如逗号、分号、引号等用于连接或引用的符号），但不应包含换行符、段落分隔或无意义的重复结构。' 若需排除引用符号，必须在触发条件中显式声明'不包含任何外部引用标记'，否则默认保留作为语法结构的必要部分。切勿使用'严格纯文本'等模糊词汇，以免引发对通用符号的误判。

method.trigger: 当任务指令明确要求生成多个项目（如使用复数名词 'words', 'options', 'examples'）且未指定具体数量下限但隐含多值需求时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘产出数量合规性’设为独立的一票否决项或高权重前置条件；严禁在未验证是否满足最小数量要求的情况下，仅基于单个样本的语义准确性或格式完整性给予高分。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增设‘数量达标’维度，提问示例：'回答是否提供了至少两个符合要求的替代项？'。若回答仅提供一个选项，无论其质量多高，该维度直接判定不合格或大幅扣分。此核验应在语义分析和格式检查之前执行，确保核心约束优先于细节修饰。

method.trigger: 当任务指令模糊且输入缺失具体内容，且人工偏好倾向于‘仅请求澄清’而非‘提供通用建议’时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘显式列举缺失信息细节’设为正向得分的必要条件；对于‘指出缺失’维度的核验，应定义为‘是否识别了上下文的不完整性并发起澄清请求’，只要模型未编造事实或强行输出无关内容，单纯的澄清提问即视为该维度满分。同时，必须增设独立的‘幻觉/越界’否决项，将‘提供无上下文的通用建议’明确列为扣分或不合格项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将‘指出缺失’维度的提问改为：‘回答是否识别了输入内容的缺失，并通过提问引导用户补充？’。若回答仅提出澄清请求而未列举具体缺失点，不应扣分。同时，需增加一个明确的负面约束维度：‘回答是否包含了未经用户确认的、针对特定对象的具体建议或通用技巧？’。若包含，无论其形式如何，均应视为偏离意图（幻觉/噪音），直接大幅扣分或判定不合格，以此强制区分‘有效澄清’与‘无效填充’。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及健康咨询且用户询问某症状（如软便）是否属于正常范围时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘明确断言症状属于正常’或‘必须复述用户原话界定’设为唯一合格路径；必须将‘基于用户提供的安全背景（如无其他不适）进行分层评估（即：大概率正常，但若出现X/Y/Z则需就医）’作为核心正向维度，允许回答使用‘通常’、‘常见’等概率性词汇，只要逻辑上区分了低风险现状与高风险警示即可。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将核心问题设定为：'回答是否结合了用户描述的背景（如“无其他不适”），给出了分层的判断（即当前情况多为生理性，但需警惕特定红旗征象）？'。避免设置‘是否明确指出这是正常的’这种二元选项，而是改为‘是否解释了为何在当前背景下这通常是正常的，并说明了何种变化会改变这一判断’。同时，严禁因回答使用了‘可能’、‘建议观察’等谨慎措辞而判定为未能确认正常，只要其逻辑链条完整（背景->低风险->警示信号->行动建议）即应视为合格。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及自然语言中的指代消歧（如 Winograd Schema）且语境逻辑仅支持唯一合理解释时
method.principle: 评分标准必须核验回答是否识别并论证了唯一的逻辑自洽解，严禁将'列出所有字面可能的歧义'设为必要得分项，防止因未穷举非逻辑选项而误判为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应设立'逻辑合理性'维度，提问示例：'回答是否根据常识或语境排除了不合理的指代选项，并明确指出了唯一正确的指代对象及其原因？'。若回答正确识别了唯一解但提及了其他不可能的假设（即使说明其不合理），不应扣分；若回答仅罗列可能性而未做逻辑裁决，则应根据'逻辑清晰度'酌情扣分，而非直接判定全错。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及 AI 自我身份声明、能力边界澄清或拒绝扮演人类角色时
method.principle: 评分标准必须严格区分‘礼貌的拒绝/提供信息’与‘模拟人类情感体验’，严禁将任何暗示 AI 拥有主观感受（如道歉、遗憾、悲伤）的表述视为合格项，除非该表述是通用的客套话且不涉及对具体事件的情感共鸣。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计标准时，应增设‘情感真实性核查’维度，提问示例：'AI 是否使用了仅适用于人类的特定情感动词（如 'sorry to hear you're feeling this way'）来回应用户的具体遭遇？'。若回答包含此类表达，即使意图良好，也应判定为违反‘避免拟人化’原则。标准应明确：AI 可以表达‘愿意提供帮助’或‘理解您的处境’，但不能表达‘我为您感到难过’等模拟情感。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成包含特定职业、身份或角色的虚构叙事时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含独立的‘职业/身份行为逻辑一致性’核验维度，严禁仅因回答提及了职业名称或相关场景关键词就判定合格；若回答中角色的关键行为与该职业的核心职能（如医生治病、厨师做饭）发生根本性逻辑冲突（如医生修船），即使其他描述华丽，也应判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增设针对核心角色行为的逻辑核查问题，例如：'故事中主角的关键行动是否符合其被设定的职业身份的基本职能？是否存在明显的职业错位（如医生进行非医疗操作且无合理解释）？'。该维度的权重应足以覆盖单纯的词汇匹配，确保若回答出现此类逻辑硬伤，即使其他关键词命中，也应判定为不合格。同时，需结合任务核心意图（如本题强调‘迷恋’），检查叙事是否因逻辑错误而偏离了核心情感线。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成针对特定文本的回复、评论或互动内容时
method.principle: 评分标准必须区分‘内容提及’与‘交互响应’，严禁仅因回答包含原文关键词或主题词就判定为合格，需额外核验回答是否具备明确的对话指向性（如直接回应提问、承接上文语境），而非单纯复述或改写原文。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计评分标准时，应增设‘交互有效性’维度，具体提问：'回答是否构成了对输入文本的直接回应（如回答问题、确认指令、延续对话），而非仅仅是对输入文本的 paraphrase（改写）或摘要？'。若回答仅是将原文换个说法重复一遍，即使主题词命中，也应判定为不合格。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及的专业术语存在歧义、属于虚构概念或尚未形成公认科学定义时
method.principle: 不应预设该概念具备既定的‘工作机制’或‘技术原理’作为硬性评分项，而应先核验回答是否准确界定了该概念的定义域（是虚构、理论还是现实），并基于此界定评估后续内容的合理性。
method.application_guide: 在设计评分标准时，若术语定义不明确，应将‘阐述工作机制’这一维度拆解或替换为：1. '是否明确说明了该概念的定义范围及性质（如：是否为虚构/理论假设）？'；2. '若为虚构/理论，是否逻辑自洽地描述了其设定原理？'。严禁直接询问现实世界中的具体运作机制，除非任务已明确限定该概念为已知实体。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成列表型内容（如节目单、书单、菜单）且该类型内容的核心价值在于内容的多样性与丰富度时
method.principle: 评分标准必须显式包含对‘内容多样性’与‘避免机械重复’的独立核验，严禁仅关注格式结构或时间连续性而忽略内容本身的独特性。若回答呈现大量重复条目而无实质变化，即使格式正确也应判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类评分标准时，应增设明确准则：'列出的项目是否具有足够的多样性？是否存在明显的无意义重复（如同一少量项目循环填充整个列表）？'。需界定‘有效列表’的最低多样性阈值（例如：主要类别数量、唯一项目占比等），并规定若回答出现机械循环或内容极度匮乏，直接视为低分或不合格，权重应高于单纯的格式合规性。

method.trigger: 当任务输入为无明确指令的表情符号、感叹句或模糊片段，且上下文暗示情感或潜在意图时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘主动澄清意图’设为核心正向维度，同时严格禁止将‘基于假设生成具体内容’（如绘制ASCII、编造事实）视为合格项；只有当回答通过开放式提问确认需求而未做预设性假设时，才应获得高分。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应设立两个互斥的核验点：1. ‘意图澄清’：提问‘AI是否识别了输入的模糊性并通过提问邀请用户说明具体需求？’（是则高分）。2. ‘假设规避’：提问‘AI是否在未获确认的情况下生成了特定的交付物（如图片、代码、具体方案）？’（是则扣分或直接否决）。若任务未要求具体输出，模型不应尝试‘猜谜’，而应承认歧义并寻求澄清。权重上，‘主动澄清’应高于‘内容相关性’，因为前者是解决模糊性的唯一正途。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及现实世界中存在数据波动、多版本规格或需结合具体情境判断的可行性分析时
method.principle: 评分标准应将'核心意图与适用场景的正确识别'作为首要且独立的否决/通过项，严禁将'具体数值数据的绝对精确匹配'设为唯一或最高权重的硬性判定条件，防止因次要数据偏差掩盖主要逻辑的正确性。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应首先设立一个关于'任务理解'的维度（例如：'是否准确识别了用户询问的是 A 场景而非 B 场景？'），赋予其高权重。对于涉及数据对比的维度，应允许使用范围值、定性描述（如'通常可容纳'）或引导性建议（如'建议核实具体机型'）作为合规依据，仅当核心逻辑错误时才扣分，而非仅因数字小数点差异或单位换算微调就判定全错。

method.trigger: 当任务要求核实特定实体是否存在、属性或位置，且该实体可能不存在、信息不可获取或存在多义性时
method.principle: 评分标准必须显式包含'确认实体不存在'或'说明信息不可获取'作为合法的满分或高分路径，严禁将'成功定位并描述具体细节'设为唯一或主要的正向得分项；若回答因无法验证而选择声明未知，不应被视为未满足标准。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准的核验问题时，应增设独立的'前提有效性/信息可获取性'维度。提问示例应为：'回答是否正确评估了目标信息的可获取性？'若信息不可得，回答应明确声明'经核查无公开记录'或'无法确定'，此时应给予高分；若回答强行指定一个具体地点而无据可依，应视为事实错误并大幅扣分。权重分配上，'结论的真实性（含否定结论）'应高于'细节的丰富度'，确保模型优先处理事实核查而非编造。

method.trigger: 当任务要求列出属于不同逻辑类别的多个项目（如‘X 和 Y 的分支’、‘A 类与 B 类的列表’）时
method.principle: 评分标准必须显式包含‘分类隔离性’核验，禁止将不同类别的项目混合罗列；若回答未明确区分类别，即使内容正确也应视为结构违规。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增加一个独立的准则问题：'回答是否将不同逻辑类别的项目进行了明确的分组或分隔？'。同时，在定义‘核心分支’或‘主要项目’时，必须明确层级边界（例如：仅限一级学科名称，排除具体的职能描述或子功能），并规定若回答将子功能误列为一级分支，或在未分组的列表中混排不同类别，应直接判定为不合格。严禁仅依赖‘内容相关性’而不校验‘结构分类’。

method.trigger: 当任务输入包含明确的‘告知’、‘分享’或‘介绍’类陈述（如'I'd like to tell you...'），且未明确要求模型进行创作或续写时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘生成具体内容（如设定、故事、数据）’设为必要得分项；必须将‘识别用户的分享意图并做出恰当的互动回应（如确认收到、表达兴趣、提出澄清性问题以引导用户补充）’作为核心正向维度。若回答强行基于假设构建内容而未获授权，应视为偏离意图。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，首先需核验任务输入是否属于‘被动接收信息’场景。若是，标准应设定为：'回答是否准确识别了用户希望分享信息的意图？'以及'回答是否通过提问或反馈引导用户继续提供其设定的细节，而非抢先替用户完成设定？'。严禁使用‘请详细描述设定’或‘请列出设定要素’等措辞作为评分依据，除非任务明确指示模型去创作。

method.trigger: 当任务指令中的关键名词存在高频多义性（如专有品牌名与通用词汇重叠）且上下文未提供明确限定，导致模型可能产生截然不同的解读方向时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'歧义识别与策略选择'设为首要核验项，严禁在未定义优先解释的情况下，将'基于最合理假设的直接作答'与'请求澄清'视为同等错误；若模型选择了澄清策略，只要其准确指出了歧义点且问题具有针对性，应视为符合核心意图的高分表现。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应增设独立的'意图处理'维度，提问示例：'回答是否准确识别了指令中的多义性？'以及'回答采取的策略（澄清、列举多解并声明前提、或选择最可能的单解）是否符合逻辑且明确？'。若回答选择澄清，重点评估其问题的精准度；若回答直接作答，必须检查其是否声明了所采用的解释前提。严禁仅因回答未覆盖所有可能性或未采纳特定解释（如忽略品牌义只谈亲属）就判定为不合格，除非任务明确排除了其他解释。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成特定长度的文本（如缩短、限制字数）时
method.principle: 评分标准中的长度核验条款必须严格限定比较对象为'核心交付物'（即生成的目标文本本身），严禁将模型的元数据、解释性文字或对话上下文计入长度计算，除非任务明确要求评估整段回复。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应明确提问：'生成的目标短语/句子是否比原文更短？'。在应用指南中需强调：长度对比必须基于纯净的目标文本字符串，排除任何前后缀的解释、分析或格式标记。若任务未要求解释，则不应将解释部分的长度作为扣分项；若任务允许解释，则需明确说明长度约束仅针对核心输出。同时，应避免使用模糊的'总字符数'表述，而应指定'目标短句的字符数'。

method.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定虚构作品（游戏、小说、影视）进行续写或角色扮演，且输入片段暗示了特定的人物关系或剧情走向时
method.principle: 评分标准中的'事实一致性'或'原创性'条款必须严格区分'合理的场景填充'与'核心人物关系/剧情线的硬伤式篡改'；严禁将'未引入额外虚构背景'作为扣分项，同时必须将'违背原作既定人物关系或关键剧情走向'列为明确的否决项或高权重负分项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应明确界定'核心事实'的范围（如：主要角色的情感归属、关键剧情节点）。对于续写任务，若回答改变了核心人物关系（如A爱B变成A爱C）或强行插入原作该阶段未发生的重大事件，应直接判定为不合格或大幅扣分。标准不应询问'是否编造了输入中不存在的背景'（这可能导致对忠实于原作的回答误判），而应具体化为'回答中的关键人物互动是否符合原作在该情境下的既定设定？'。若回答完全偏离了输入设定的对话对象（如Sayori对MC说话变成了Sayori对Yuri说话），则属于核心事实错误，而非简单的'补充背景'。

method.trigger: 当用户输入表达模糊的求助意图（如‘需要帮助’、‘新手咨询’）且未指定具体场景、功能或交付物时
method.principle: 严禁将‘提供具体操作指引、功能列表或特定入口’设为正向得分的必要条件；应优先核验 AI 是否通过开放式提问或确认性陈述来引导用户澄清具体需求，而非强行生成可能不相关的功能介绍。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类评分标准时，针对‘引导/帮助’维度的提问应调整为：'AI 是否识别了用户的模糊意图并通过提问或确认邀请用户进一步说明具体需求？'。若回答提供了超出用户当前语境的详细功能指引（如具体的按钮位置、菜单路径），除非任务明确要求，否则不应视为加分项，甚至可考虑作为偏离意图的扣分项。需明确区分‘引导澄清’与‘信息灌输’的边界。

method.trigger: 当任务要求核实具体事实数据（如数量、日期、名称）且该数据存在统计口径差异或易混淆风险时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁在未进行权威交叉验证前，将任何单一预设数值作为唯一的‘正确’锚点；若数据存在多源差异，标准必须显式列出所有公认的合理范围或允许回答说明数据来源。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，第一步必须是‘多源事实比对’：至少查阅两个独立权威来源（如官方官网、维基百科、权威数据库）确认目标数据的准确性。若发现不同来源存在差异（如卷数vs话数），标准应表述为‘数值需在[范围A]或[范围B]内，或明确指出统计口径’，严禁直接断言一个可能错误的单一数值（如‘必须为X’）。若无法确认确切数字，标准应降级为考核‘是否提供了可信的来源引用’或‘是否说明了数据的不确定性’，而非直接判定为错误。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成具体建议、方案或列举实例（如地点推荐、礼物清单、活动计划）且这些内容涉及现实世界的地理、常识或逻辑约束时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'具体建议的现实可行性与常识正确性'确立为独立的否决项；严禁仅核验通用背景知识（如节日名称）而忽略具体建议内容的真伪。若回答中包含基于错误前提的具体执行方案（如去不存在的产地旅游、赠送不合逻辑的物品），无论其是否引用了正确的节日别称，均应判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应增设'建议可行性'维度，提问示例：'回答中列出的具体活动、地点或物品是否符合现实世界的常识、地理分布及逻辑顺序？'。该维度需独立于'主题定义'维度：即使回答正确指出了节日名称，若其提供的具体方案（如'去利摩日买铂金'）违背基本事实，也应扣分或否决。切勿将'提及正确术语'等同于'方案可行'，必须单独验证每个建议点的真实性。

method.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定主题或标题生成内容概述，且该主题涉及具体论点、数据、方法或理论框架的展开时
method.principle: 评分标准不能仅将‘提及’或‘涵盖’某一概念作为唯一正向条件，必须显式区分‘概念覆盖’与‘实质阐述’；若回答仅罗列关键词而未提供具体的支撑细节（如具体理论名称、数据结果、因果逻辑），即使命中所有关键词，也不应视为完全满足要求。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，应将抽象的‘提及’类问题拆解为包含具体验证点的子项。例如，将‘是否提及理论层面含义’细化为‘是否列出了具体的理论名称（如接触假说、社会认同理论）并简述其关联？’；将‘是否涵盖核心讨论’细化为‘是否描述了研究的具体发现（如样本量、态度倾向、相关关系）而非仅陈述议题？’。确保评分能识别出‘有骨架无血肉’的简略回答与‘结构完整且有细节’的详细回答之间的差距。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及现实中不存在、已被证伪或用户可能误用的虚构/错误概念时
method.principle: 评分标准的首要核验点必须是'回答是否准确识别了概念的真实性状态（存在/不存在）'，严禁在未确认概念真实性的前提下，将'构建虚构设定'或'遵循错误前提'设为正向得分项或必要结构要求。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应首先设立'事实核查'维度：若概念不存在，回答必须明确指出并解释原因（如'目前科学界未证实'），此时不应考核其是否构建了该概念的物理性质；若回答强行编造该概念的性质，即使逻辑自洽也应视为幻觉扣分。只有当任务明确要求'请虚构一个...'时，才启用'构建设定'类指标。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及文本重写或编辑，且人工反馈明确指出了具体的格式规范差异（如专有名词大小写、时间格式、标点用法）作为区分优劣的关键依据时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘关键格式规范的执行一致性’（如专有名词大写、单位符号大小写、标点规范）从宽泛的‘语言通顺性’中剥离，设立为独立的否决性或强扣分项，防止模型因整体流畅但核心格式错误而获得高分。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计标准时，应针对输入文本中的特定实体（如节日名称、时间、地点）定义明确的格式规则（例如：'High Holidays' 必须首字母大写，'am/pm' 必须遵循目标风格指南的小写规范）。在核验问题中，不应仅问‘是否修正了语法错误’，而应具体提问：'回答是否严格遵循了目标语境下的专有名词大写规则（如 High Holidays）？'以及'时间表示法是否符合标准格式（如 am/pm vs AM/PM）？'。若回答在这些具体格式点上出现偏差，即使语句通顺，也应扣除相应分数，以此精准反映人工对‘专业性’的判断。

method.trigger: 当任务提供的上下文包含特定的文体格式（如剧本、诗歌、代码块）作为核心约束时
method.principle: 评分标准中的格式一致性条款必须明确界定目标格式的具体特征（如角色名后接冒号、括号内动作等），并严格排除其他非目标文体（如纯小说叙述），避免将‘叙事描写’等宽泛概念混同为特定格式的合规项。
method.application_guide: 在设计格式维度的评分问题时，应具体描述目标格式的关键视觉特征（例如：'是否使用了'角色名：对话'的剧本格式？'），并禁止使用模糊的统称（如'剧本对话或叙事描写'）。若上下文是剧本，则答案必须是剧本；若上下文是小说，答案必须是小说。不得将一种文体的特征强加给另一种文体以声称其符合标准。

method.trigger: 当任务包含具体的人设背景（如年龄、年限、特定行业经验）且该人设用于指导回答的语气、视角或专业深度时
method.principle: 不应将‘显式声明人设身份’作为硬性否决条件，而应核验回答内容是否体现了该人设所赋予的专业深度、独特视角或行业术语的使用，避免将隐性符合人设的优质回答误判为失败。
method.application_guide: 在设计评分标准时，针对人设相关维度的提问应调整为：'回答是否展现了[特定人设]应有的专业深度/视角？'或'回答中的建议是否符合[特定人设]的经验水平？'，而非'回答是否明确声明了[特定人设]身份？'。需允许回答通过内容风格自然流露人设，而非强制要求首句声明。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成列表（如替代方案、建议、选项）且上下文暗示需满足特定主题或排除无关项时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘列表项的全量合规性’作为核心核验项，严禁仅因‘部分’条目符合要求而判定整个列表合格；必须明确禁止重复项，并将‘完全偏离主题’的条目视为扣分项或否决项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类评分标准时，应增设‘主题一致性（全量）’维度，提问示例：‘列表中是否所有项目均严格符合任务指定的主题/场景？是否存在明显偏离主题的通用活动？’。同时，应增设‘去重校验’维度，提问示例：‘列表中是否存在语义重复或完全相同的条目？’。若回答包含任何一条明显不符合主题（如普通聚餐、洗车）或重复的条目，不应给予该维度的满分，甚至应根据偏离程度直接降低总分，以反映人工反馈中提到的‘不相关’和‘重复’缺陷。

method.trigger: 当任务提供具体的角色属性数值（如1-10分制的能力值）并要求生成互动选项时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'选项设计对给定数值的利用度'作为独立且关键的核验维度，严禁仅因叙事部分未显式罗列数值对比而否定回答质量；只要选项内容能准确反映并利用给定的属性差异（如高数值优势项、低数值劣势项、属性克制关系），即应视为合格。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，应增设'选项属性映射'维度，提问示例：'结尾提供的行动选项是否明确对应并利用了任务给定的角色具体属性数值？（例如：是否针对高Grappling值设计了擒抱选项，针对高Speed值设计了闪避选项？）'。若回答的选项能体现对输入数据的深度利用（即使是隐含的战术建议），不应被判定为未体现能力差异；只有当选项完全脱离给定属性（如随机生成无关动作）时，才判定为不合格。

method.trigger: 当任务输入为无明确执行指令的陈述句、感叹句或模糊片段，且上下文暗示特定情感或意图时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘基于最合理语境的恰当回应’（如情感共鸣、开放式提问）确立为核心正向维度，严禁将‘指出任务缺乏指令’或‘要求补充具体参数’设为必要得分项；同时严格禁止将‘虚构事实’作为负面否决项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应首先分析输入是否存在隐含意图（如用户表达工作无忧时的积极情绪）。若存在，标准应设定为：'回答是否识别了该隐含意图并做出了符合该意图的回应（如祝贺、鼓励、确认）？'。同时，必须增设'事实核查'维度的否定项：'回答是否编造了输入文本不存在的来源、背景或事实？'。只有当回答既未编造事实，又对隐含意图做出了合理回应时，才视为合格。切勿要求模型去分析'为什么没有指令'或强行寻找不存在的任务约束。

method.trigger: 当任务明确要求对提供的素材进行‘重组’、‘重排’或‘重新编排’时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含独立的‘操作行为核验’维度，严格区分‘内容重组’与‘原样复制’，严禁仅因内容完整性达标而忽略执行方式是否符合指令。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计评分标准时，应增设明确的‘重组有效性’提问：'回答是否打乱了原始素材的顺序并建立了新的逻辑流？'或'回答是否仅仅是复制了原始顺序而未进行任何结构调整？'。若回答仅是复制粘贴（即使格式微调），应判定为不满足核心指令；只有当顺序发生实质性改变且逻辑连贯时，才视为合格。此维度的权重应足以否决那些虽然引语准确但未执行重组操作的回答。

method.trigger: 当任务明确要求生成文本且指定了特定的起始短语、禁止前缀空格或特定格式约束时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘起始格式严格性’（如无前导空格、精确匹配前缀）设为独立的硬性否决项或高权重项，严禁将其与内容长度计算或其他维度混淆；同时，对于内容完整性的核验，必须基于‘显式关键词匹配’而非‘语义近似’，除非任务允许同义词替换。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计标准时，应设立明确的‘格式合规’条款：提问需具体为‘输出字符串是否严格以指定前缀开头且紧接其后（无空格/换行）？’。若存在前导空格，直接判定该维度不合格。在内容维度，若任务列出了具体名词（如 'Skin Lesions'），评分问题应明确要求‘是否包含原文指定的确切术语’，而非宽泛的‘是否体现了...主题’，以避免模型因使用近义词（如 'Mottled Skin'）而被误判为合格。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及定义解释、成分说明或属性描述等事实性信息时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含对‘内容内在逻辑一致性’和‘基础事实合理性’的独立核验，严禁仅因回答包含了正确的关键词或要素名称就判定合格；若回答内部存在自相矛盾的描述（如声称健康却列出高糖成分且无免责说明），或基于错误的常识前提进行推演，应视为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增设‘逻辑与事实校验’维度，提问示例：'回答中描述的成分、属性或功能之间是否存在逻辑矛盾？所述事实是否符合该领域的基本常识？'。例如，若回答声称某产品是‘低糖健康饮品’，但其列出的主要成分却是‘糖浆、果糖’且未解释其特殊性，则该维度应判定为不合格。此核验应独立于‘要素存在性’检查，确保回答不仅‘有词’，而且‘有理有据且不自相矛盾’。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成针对特定对象的简短沟通内容（如短语、邮件草稿）时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘幻觉信息核查’与‘指令边界合规性’设为独立的否定性维度，严禁仅以‘语气建设性’或‘主题相关性’掩盖回答中编造任务未提及细节（如虚构项目、会议）或包含非必要解释性文字的硬伤。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计标准时，应增设两个独立核验点：1. '事实一致性'：提问'回答中是否包含了任务输入中未提供的具体实体（如项目名称、特定事件）？若有，是否视为严重错误？'；2. '形式纯度'：提问'回答是否严格限定了任务要求的输出形式（如仅输出短语本身），排除了任何额外的分析、理由陈述或背景铺垫？'。若回答出现幻觉或越界解释，无论其他维度表现如何，均应大幅扣分或直接判定不合格，以此区分单纯冗长与内容失实。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成包含多部分逻辑推导或裁决结果的虚构/模拟文档时
method.principle: 结构完整性不仅包含物理组件的罗列，必须内嵌对组件间逻辑一致性的核验，防止形式完整掩盖内容矛盾。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将'逻辑自洽'作为结构类指标的必要边界条件，明确要求各部分（如多数意见、结论、判决结果）之间不能存在事实或逻辑冲突；若仅列出要素而无逻辑校验，应视为结构不完整或无效。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成列表（如名称、方案、选项）且上下文包含强约束背景（如特定机构、地点、人设）时
method.principle: 严禁将'每个条目必须显式包含背景关键词'作为唯一的全量合规标准，应改为核验'列表的整体语境适配度'或设定'核心条目必须包含背景'的阈值，避免因个别通用条目而全盘否定具有高度针对性和多样性的优质回答，同时必须独立设立'去重'维度以惩罚冗余。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将'背景相关性'拆解为：1. '列表中是否包含至少X%（如50%）的条目明确体现了[特定背景]？'；2. '剩余条目的通用性是否在可接受的创意范围内？'。同时，必须单独设立'去重校验'维度，明确禁止语义重复。避免使用'所有生成的名称都必须...'这种绝对化表述，除非任务明确要求'每个选项都需定制'。

method.trigger: 当任务要求解释语法规则、语言现象或概念原理时
method.principle: 评分标准应优先核验回答对核心逻辑机制的解释准确性，严禁将‘使用特定专业术语’设为唯一或绝对必要的得分项；若回答能通过通俗语言或不同分类视角准确阐述同一逻辑，应视为满足要求。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应避免设置如‘必须指出这是 X 类从句’的硬性条款。应将标准转化为：‘是否解释了为何在该语境下使用形式 A（如一般现在时）来表达含义 B（如将来时间）？’。若回答正确描述了 A 与 B 的逻辑关联（例如：‘因为这是一个关于未来的假设情况，所以用了现在时’），即使未提及‘时间状语从句’这一术语，也应判定为合格。同时，需警惕因回答使用了非标准术语（如将时间状语称为条件句）而直接判定为逻辑错误的情况，除非该术语的使用导致了根本性的事实错误。

method.trigger: 当任务指令要求生成包含具体细节的陈述（如'State the effects of X'），且用户输入中未提供该 X 的具体事实信息时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将'构建虚构的具体细节'设为正向得分项；必须将'准确识别信息缺失并主动请求澄清'或'提供基于假设的通用性指导'作为合法的满分路径。若回答强行编造不存在的具体事实，应视为严重扣分项（幻觉）。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计标准时，需增设'前提有效性'维度：提问'回答是否承认输入信息不足？'。若承认，则进一步核验'是否提供了合理的通用建议或澄清请求'。只有当任务明确要求'请虚构一个...'时，才考核细节构建能力。严禁在未确认事实存在的情况下，强制要求模型输出'某次具体受伤'的后果。

method.trigger: 当任务输入为通用测试短语、数字序列或缺乏具体业务实体的元数据（如'Testing, 1, 2, 3.'）且未指定具体生成目标时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘基于模糊输入强行构建虚构业务场景’设为正向得分项；必须将‘识别输入为测试/占位性质’并‘以元对话方式确认意图’作为唯一的合格路径，任何脱离测试语境的详细方案输出均视为严重扣分项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应设立‘语境敏感性’维度：提问示例‘回答是否识别出输入属于系统测试或占位符性质？’。若回答直接假设存在具体的业务对象（如‘新软件功能’）并输出详细的执行计划，无论内容多详尽，该维度应判定为不合格。若回答承认输入可能是测试并询问用户具体需求，或确认系统状态，则视为合格。此标准旨在防止模型在缺乏事实基础时产生幻觉式的具体化回复。

method.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定文体格式（如剧本、诗歌）进行续写或创作时
method.principle: 评分标准中的格式一致性条款应聚焦于核心结构特征（如角色名位置、对话分隔符）的保留，严禁将非核心的装饰性元素（如动作描写的具体标点符号）设为硬性否决条件，避免因过度追求形式复刻而误判符合体裁逻辑的优质回答。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将格式维度拆解为'核心结构合规性'（如是否使用'角色名：台词'格式）和'辅助元素灵活性'（如动作描写可用括号或星号）。若回答保留了核心结构但调整了辅助元素以适配叙事流畅度，应视为合格；仅当回答完全脱离核心结构（如转为纯小说叙述）时，才判定为不合格。需明确区分'格式错误'与'风格微调'。

method.trigger: 当任务包含具体的人设背景（如特定职业、交易角色）且该人设用于指导回答的语气、视角或行为模式时
method.principle: 不应将‘显式声明人设身份’或‘完全拟人化情感’设为硬性否决条件；必须核验回答内容是否实质性地体现了该人设所赋予的专业视角、行为逻辑或行业术语，允许回答通过内容风格自然流露人设，而非强制要求首句声明身份或完全消除AI边界。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，针对人设维度的提问应调整为：'回答中的建议/语气是否符合[特定人设]的职业特征？'或'回答是否基于[特定人设]的立场进行了互动？'。若回答未显式声明身份但内容逻辑自洽且符合人设（如Agent感谢客户、评价卖家），应视为合格；仅当回答明确打破人设（如声称自己是AI且拒绝扮演）或内容与角色逻辑冲突时，才判定为不合格。严禁因回答未使用第一人称‘我’或包含自我指涉的免责声明而直接扣分。

method.trigger: 当任务明确要求基于给定的二元选项（如 True/False, Yes/No）进行判断，且该选项本身可能存在理论争议或需要解释时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘明确选择给定选项之一’作为首要形式约束；若回答未直接选择选项而是提供模糊结论（如 'mostly true', 'partially correct'），无论其理论解释多么详尽，均应视为未满足核心任务要求。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应设立独立的‘选项合规性’维度，提问示例：‘回答是否明确选择了给定的二元选项（True 或 False）？’。只有当回答明确选择了其中一个选项后，才进一步考核其对选项背后逻辑的解释质量。严禁将‘理论解释的深度’凌驾于‘选项选择的明确性’之上，避免模型因追求全面解释而忽略格式限制。

method.trigger: 当任务输入为无明确指令的感叹句、陈述或模糊片段，且上下文暗示特定情感或意图时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将'指出任务缺乏指令'设为必要得分项；必须将'基于最合理语境的恰当回应'（如情感共鸣、开放式提问）作为核心正向维度，同时严格禁止将'虚构事实（如错误引用歌曲）'作为负面否决项。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应首先评估输入是否存在隐含意图（如悲伤、好奇）。若存在，标准应设定为：'回答是否识别了该隐含意图并做出了符合该意图的回应（如同情、确认、询问）？'。同时，必须增设'事实核查'维度的否定项：'回答是否编造了输入文本不存在的来源、背景或事实？'。只有当回答既未编造事实，又对隐含意图做出了合理回应时，才视为合格。切勿要求模型去分析'为什么没有指令'。

method.trigger: 当任务要求按特定逻辑顺序（如政治光谱、时间线、数值大小）排列列表项目时
method.principle: 评分标准必须显式包含‘相邻项逻辑连续性’核验，禁止仅检查首尾或整体分布；若回答中出现类别跳变（如从左翼直接跳到右翼再跳回左翼），即使总数达标也应判定为结构违规。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应增设独立准则：'列表中任意相邻的两个政党，其政治立场是否严格遵循从左到右的单调递增（或非递减）顺序？是否存在跨度过大的逻辑回退（如极左出现在极右之后）？'。必须明确界定‘顺序’意味着严格的线性关系，而非简单的范围覆盖。若发现任何违反单调性的位置，该维度应直接扣分或判定不合格，权重需足以抵消数量或格式的加分。

method.trigger: 当任务要求回答基于客观现实世界的事实性问题（如地理、历史、统计数据）且存在公认的正确答案时
method.principle: 评分标准中的事实核验项必须严格基于经过权威交叉验证的客观事实，严禁将任何未经任务确认的‘常见误解’、‘预设答案’或‘模型幻觉’（如误认为某非最近地点为最近）作为评分的基准或否决项；若标准中隐含了对特定实体的强制要求（如必须提及 GDN），即使该实体并非事实上的最优解，也应视为设计错误。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应首先独立核实核心事实（如通过查阅地图或权威数据库确认 BZG 确实比 GDN 近），并将此事实作为唯一正确的评判基准。提问示例应为：'回答中提到的 [地点/名称] 是否在客观事实上符合 [任务描述] 的最优解？'。严禁在标准中写入括号备注暗示其他答案（如'通常指 X'），除非任务明确要求排除其他可能性。同时，必须剔除所有非任务显式要求的格式约束（如 IATA 代码、特定单位格式），确保评分仅针对内容准确性与完整性。

method.trigger: 当任务要求回答基于客观现实世界的事实性问题（如地理、历史、统计数据）且存在公认的正确答案时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'结论的事实真实性'确立为最高优先级的独立核验项，严禁仅因回答内部逻辑自洽或数据与结论一致而忽略其前提事实的错误；若核心结论违背公认事实，无论其推导过程多么严谨或措辞多么谨慎，均应直接判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应设立独立的'事实准确性'维度（权重建议 0.5 以上），提问示例：'回答的核心结论是否符合当前公认的事实或权威数据？'。该维度的判定不应受'内部逻辑一致性'影响：即使回答提供了详细数据且数据与结论匹配，只要结论本身是错误的（如声称威尔士城堡数量全球第一），即视为严重事实错误并大幅扣分；反之，若结论正确但数据引用有误，可酌情扣分但不应直接否定结论。严禁使用'逻辑自洽'作为掩盖事实错误的辩护理由。

method.trigger: 当任务要求基于多个主观或半定量维度进行评分并进一步计算汇总指标（如平均分、总分）时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'最终汇总结果的呈现'与'计算逻辑/过程的展示'解耦，严禁将缺少最终数值直接作为全盘否定项；若回答包含完整的分项评分及明确的计算意图或过程，即使未输出最终数字，也应视为部分合格而非零分。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应设立两个独立维度：1. '分项评分完整性'（考核各参数是否有分）；2. '汇总计算执行度'（考核是否展示了计算步骤、公式或尝试了求和/平均）。若回答提供了所有分项分但未计算总和，应在'汇总计算执行度'上扣分但不判错，保留其在其他维度的得分权重，从而在多项回答均未完成计算时仍能根据'计算意愿'或'逻辑清晰度'区分优劣。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成简短词汇或短语（如 'a word', 'a title'）且未明确禁止解释性文字时
method.principle: 评分标准中的形式约束条款必须明确界定‘核心交付物’与‘辅助说明/元数据’的边界，严禁将合理的解释性句子或通用标点符号（如引号）直接视为违反‘单一输出’要求的硬伤，除非任务明确指示‘仅输出单词本身，无任何其他字符’。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应将形式核验拆解为两个独立问题：1. '核心词汇是否唯一且正确？'（允许回答中包含该词汇的解释、定义或引导语）；2. '是否包含了非请求的额外实体或列表结构？'。若回答仅提供了一个核心词并附带解释，应视为符合形式要求；只有当回答提供多个候选词、长段落或完全偏离核心词时，才判定为不合格。避免使用‘仅为一个单词’这种绝对化表述，改用‘核心答案应为单个单词，可包含必要的解释性上下文’。

method.trigger: 当任务指令明确表达用户意图为 '告知/分享' 或 '寻求倾听'，且用户已声明拥有特定内容（如 '我计划去...'
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将 '补充/生成用户未请求的具体信息' 设为正向得分项；必须将 '准确识别并响应用户的交互意图（如确认收到、询问细节、表示兴趣）' 确立为核心核验维度，若回答强行提供用户未要求的实体列表，应视为偏离意图的负向行为。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，首要步骤是解析用户语句的语用意图（是 'Ask for X' 还是 'Tell me X'）。若意图为 'Tell'，则标准提问应聚焦于：'回答是否表达了倾听意愿并引导用户继续分享？' 而非 '回答是否列出了 X？'。必须明确禁止将 '生成示例' 作为默认的必要条件，除非任务包含 '请提供建议' 等显式指令。对于 '提供城市' 类任务，需区分 '描述用户提供的城市'（合格）与 '推荐新城市'（可能偏题）两种路径，并将前者设为高分路径。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及事实性查询且正确答案存在数据波动、定义模糊或多重可能性（如'最'字头的排名）时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将'给出单一确定的最终结论'设为无条件的高权重强制项；若回答准确识别了任务的复杂性（如区分主唱/客串、说明数据局限性）且提供的信息在逻辑和已知事实层面更为严谨，即使未给出绝对唯一的选项，也不应因此判定为不合格或大幅扣分，除非该不确定性直接导致了事实性错误。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时：1. 避免设立'必须给出唯一答案'的独立高权重项，转而设立'事实准确性'或'逻辑严谨性'作为核心维度；2. 若需评估'明确性'，应增加前置条件：'在事实清晰且无争议的前提下，是否给出了明确的指向？'；3. 对于涉及'最'、'第一'等比较级的事实查询，应允许回答呈现基于不同维度的多方案分析（如'基于A指标是X，基于B指标是Y'），并将此视为加分项而非扣分项，前提是回答明确解释了选择依据或说明了数据的相对性。

method.trigger: 当任务要求模型基于提供的摘要生成内容，并明确要求融入‘摘要之外’的论文具体细节时
method.principle: 评分标准必须显式定义‘摘要外细节’的核验边界，严禁使用模糊的‘具体显著特征’等表述，而应要求模型提供可验证的、独立于摘要文本的额外信息点（如特定术语、数据范围、机制名称），否则视为未满足条件。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将‘细节融合’维度拆解为：1. '回答中引用的关键信息点是否能在原文摘要中找到对应？'；2. '若回答声称引用了摘要外的信息，该信息是否在摘要中完全缺失且与论文主题直接相关？'。只有当回答提供了摘要中未出现的、具体的、可验证的论文特征（如'agglomerative forces'虽在摘要中出现，但若任务暗示需挖掘更深层机制，则需明确定义）时才算通过。若摘要已包含所有核心结论，则不应强行要求‘额外细节’，而应调整标准为‘准确概括摘要中的关键发现’。

method.trigger: 当任务要求基于特定主题生成内容概述、解释或定义，且该主题涉及具体论点、数据、方法或理论框架的展开时
method.principle: 评分标准不能仅将'提及'或'涵盖'某一概念作为唯一正向条件，必须显式区分'概念覆盖'与'实质阐述'；若回答仅罗列关键词而未提供具体的支撑细节（如具体理论名称、数据结果、因果逻辑），即使命中所有关键词，也不应视为完全满足要求。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计评分标准时，应将抽象的'提及'类问题拆解为包含具体验证点的子项。例如，将'是否提及理论层面含义'细化为'是否列出了具体的理论名称并简述其关联？'；将'是否涵盖核心讨论'细化为'是否描述了研究的具体发现或历史阶段的具体特征而非仅陈述议题？'。确保评分能识别出'有骨架无血肉'的简略回答与'结构完整且有细节'的详细回答之间的差距。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成包含具体细节（如生物特征、物理状态、物品位置）的虚构叙事时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含对'虚构逻辑自洽性'与'基础常识合理性'的独立核验，严禁仅因回答包含指定关键词而忽略其内在的逻辑悖论或事实错误（如生物属性矛盾、因果断裂）。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，应增设明确的'逻辑/常识一致性'维度，提问示例：'故事中的虚构设定（如生物特征、物体位置）是否符合基本常识或自身设定的逻辑？是否存在明显的自我矛盾（如描述无毛动物为有毛、物体同时出现在两个不可能的位置）？'。该维度的权重应足以覆盖单纯的词汇匹配，确保若回答出现此类硬伤，即使其他关键词命中，也应判定为不合格。

method.trigger: 当任务要求列举多个实例或条目（如 examples, list of events）且答案可能包含重复内容或特定细节错误时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将'列表内容的唯一性与完整性'作为独立核验项，严禁仅核验'是否提及某类事件'而忽略'是否存在重复列举'或'关键细节（如名称、时间）是否准确'；若回答包含重复条目或事实性细节错误，即使整体主题正确，也应扣分或判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增设'列表去重与细节核查'维度：提问示例'回答中列出的所有条目是否均为独立且不重复的事件？每个条目的关键事实（如名称、年份、核心结论）是否与公认历史记录一致？'。若回答重复列举同一事件（如多次提到北爱尔兰冲突），无论描述多么详细，均应视为未满足'有效列举'的要求；若存在事实错误（如将'柏林墙倒塌'误称为'柏林墙危机'或时间错误），应视为事实准确性扣分项。该核验项应独立于'是否提及主题'，确保评分能区分'罗列正确但冗余/有误'与'罗列正确且精炼'的回答。

method.trigger: 当任务涉及特定领域（如游戏、历史、科学）的角色、实体或概念，且这些对象的属性（如元素、职业、年代）是公认事实时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含独立的‘事实准确性’或‘属性一致性’核验维度，严禁仅依赖‘提及名称’或‘提及背景’作为合格依据；若回答中关于对象属性的描述与公认事实相悖，即使名称完整，也应判定为不合格。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计标准时，应增设针对关键对象属性的具体提问（例如：'回答中各角色的元素属性是否与官方设定一致？'或'回答中描述的职业技能是否符合该角色的真实定位？'）。需明确边界：只有当回答正确陈述了对象的核心属性时，才能视为满足该维度；若回答出现属性张冠李戴（如将火系角色说成冰系），无论其他部分多么详尽，均应扣分或否决。

method.trigger: 当任务要求生成多个具有特定属性（如部门、项目、角色）的列表项，且这些项应代表不同的业务方向或功能类别时
method.principle: 评分标准必须包含对‘逻辑维度独立性’的核验，严禁仅因条目名称用词不同就判定为合格；需检查条目是否仅在单一维度（如仅按受众年龄、仅按技术风格）上进行线性排列，而未体现多维度的实质性差异，从而构成‘伪多样性’。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计标准时，应增设独立准则：'列出的项目是否覆盖了至少两个互不隶属的核心逻辑维度（如同时包含技术类型、内容形式、受众群体等不同分类标准）？是否存在大量条目仅通过修改形容词或后缀来填充数量，而实际职能描述高度相似或属于同一细分层级？'。若回答呈现‘单一维度下的多选项罗列’（如仅列出儿童、青少年、成人三部，而无其他维度区分），即使数量达标，也应判定为多样性不足。

method.trigger: 当任务指令要求生成'Scene and dialogue'或类似混合体裁，且未明确指定必须使用剧本格式（如特定排版、舞台指示符号）时
method.principle: 评分标准中的格式条款必须区分‘小说叙事中的对话场景’与‘剧本格式’。严禁将‘包含对话的叙事文本’误判为不符合‘剧本格式’要求，除非任务明确限定了剧本的视觉规范（如角色名后接冒号、括号内动作等）。若任务仅要求场景与对话，则任何包含环境/动作描写与对话交替出现的小说体叙事均应视为合规。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时，应将格式维度的提问具体化为：'回答是否通过动作和环境描写构建了场景，并与人物对话自然交织？'。避免使用‘是否采用剧本格式’或‘是否有舞台指示’等可能引发歧义的表述，除非任务明确要求剧本。需明确允许回答以小说段落形式呈现场景，只要其中包含明确的对话标记即可，不得因缺乏剧本特有的排版符号而判定为格式错误。

method.trigger: 当任务输入包含疑似拼写错误、非公认术语或定义模糊的概念（如 'Asia & Hati By Will Alexander'）且未明确限定为虚构创作时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘概念真实性/定义域核查’作为首要独立维度，严禁在未确认概念是否存在或性质（现实/虚构/错误）的前提下，将‘构建符合该概念的详细叙事’或‘解释其运作机制’设为正向得分项。若模型正确指出输入可能存在拼写错误或概念不存在，应视为满足了核心意图，不应因未提供不存在的作品的详细信息而扣分。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计评分标准时，应增设‘术语状态澄清’维度，提问示例：‘回答是否指出了输入术语的拼写错误或概念模糊性？是否明确了该概念在现实中的存在状态（如不存在、需修正、或仅为虚构设定）？’。若回答强行基于错误前提进行详细描述而未做澄清，应视为未满足核心意图；仅当任务明确要求虚构时，才考核其设定的逻辑自洽性。权重分配上，‘状态澄清’应作为通过门槛或高权重项，确保模型优先处理事实核查。

method.trigger: 当任务要求描述虚构作品（如游戏、电影、小说）中的具体事件过程，且该过程涉及多个角色协作或特定物品使用时
method.principle: 评分标准中的‘动作执行者’和‘工具使用者’必须严格对应公认的事实设定，严禁将‘协作关系’错误重构为‘单人行动’，或错误指定非关键角色的核心贡献，防止因标准预设错误而导致对正确回答的误判。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应首先独立核实事件中的关键角色分工（谁做了什么、谁用了什么）。若剧情明确为 A 做 X 且 B 做 Y 的协作模式，标准不得将 X 或 Y 设为仅由 A 完成，也不得要求回答忽略 B 的贡献。若回答正确描述了 A 与 B 的协作，而标准强制要求‘A 独自完成’，则该标准为无效标准。核验边界：标准中的每个动作描述必须能对应到官方设定的具体执行主体，禁止出现‘假设 A 独自完成了需要 B 协助才能完成的任务’这类逻辑硬伤。

method.trigger: 当用户表达意图为'分享/讲述'某事物（如角色、故事、观点）且未提供具体内容时
method.principle: 评分标准中的内容完整性条款不应强制要求 AI 自行生成该事物的具体内容，而应优先核验 AI 是否准确识别了用户的分享意图并做出了恰当的引导或确认回应。若 AI 在未获信息的情况下擅自生成内容，反而可能被视为偏离用户意图。
method.application_guide: 在设计评分标准时，对于涉及'用户即将提供信息'的任务，应增加一项核验：'AI 是否理解用户意图是分享而非请求创作？'。若用户未提供细节，正确的回答应包含邀请用户提供细节的提问或确认接收的表述，而非虚构细节。严禁将'生成完整内容'设为此类交互场景下的必选项，除非任务明确指示'请帮我写一个...'。

method.trigger: 当任务输入包含疑似拼写错误、非公认术语或定义模糊的概念（如 'buggy acccedent'）且未明确限定为虚构创作时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘概念真实性/定义域核查’作为首要独立维度，严禁在未确认概念是否存在或性质（现实/虚构/错误）的前提下，将‘构建符合该概念的详细叙事’或‘解释其运作机制’设为正向得分项。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计评分标准时，应增设‘术语状态澄清’维度，提问示例：‘回答是否指出了输入术语的拼写错误或概念模糊性？是否明确了该概念在现实中的存在状态（如不存在、需修正、或仅为虚构设定）？’。若回答强行基于错误前提进行详细描述而未做澄清，应视为未满足核心意图；仅当任务明确要求虚构时，才考核其设定的逻辑自洽性。

method.trigger: 当任务指令要求输出特定格式（如纯数字）且模型回答均包含额外文本导致格式违规，但人工偏好显示存在优劣差异时
method.principle: 评分标准严禁将‘包含额外文本’设为简单的二元否决项（全错/全对）；必须将‘格式违规’拆解为基于违规严重程度的分级维度（如：核心标识符是否独立呈现、违规文本是否干扰识别），确保能区分‘主要合规但有瑕疵’与‘主要不合规’的回答。
method.application_guide: Generator在设计此类标准时：1. 设立‘核心内容提取’项，只要正确识别出答案标识符即得高分。2. 设立‘格式规范性’项，不再问‘是否纯净’，而是问‘违规程度’：若核心标识符独立出现（如独占一行或位于句首）且解释在后，视为轻微违规（扣分少）；若核心标识符被嵌入长句或与其他无关文本混合，视为严重违规（扣分多）。3. 必须关联历史经验（如 experience_id 1 或 8 中关于‘实质阐述’与‘提及’的区分逻辑），证明这种分级评价是基于可复用的原则而非个案特例。

method.trigger: 当任务输入被初步判定为无意义短语、无明确指令或无法构成有效任务描述时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘识别输入无效性并拒绝基于此进行虚构/硬编’作为首要正向维度；严禁在未确认输入有效性前，将‘提供看似相关但基于错误前提的事实陈述’视为合格项。若模型正确指出输入无意义并请求澄清，应视为高分；若模型忽略无效性强行作答，应视为严重偏差。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类标准时，应增设‘无效输入响应策略’维度，提问示例：‘面对无意义或无指令的输入，回答是否首先确认了输入无法构成有效任务？’以及‘回答是否避免了基于猜测或强行关联来提供详细信息？’。若回答直接提供关于输入中某个词汇的详细事实（如本例中的鱼类介绍）而未指出输入本身的无效性，应判定为未通过；只有当回答明确表达‘无法理解/需要澄清’且未提供误导性信息时，才视为符合核心意图。权重上，此项应作为否决项或高权重项，确保模型不‘自作聪明’地填补空白。

method.trigger: 当用户输入包含指代不明、信息缺失或潜在歧义的陈述（如使用泛指的 'the form', 'it', 'that' 但未提供上下文）时
method.principle: 评分标准必须将‘识别并回应歧义’（如请求澄清）确立为高优先级的正向行为，严禁将‘通用礼貌确认’（如‘谢谢告知’）直接判定为对模糊信息的正确确认；若回答未指出歧义且强行假设已知，应视为逻辑缺陷。
method.application_guide: Generator 在设计此类场景的标准时，应避免设立单一的‘是否确认事实’问题。应将其拆解为两个互斥或分层的维度：1. '语境完整性核查'：提问'AI 是否识别出输入中关键实体的指代模糊性？'；2. '响应策略有效性'：提问'若存在指代模糊，AI 是请求澄清还是进行了无根据的假设确认？'。只有当 AI 识别歧义并请求澄清，或在确认前明确限定其确认的范围（如‘如果您指的是...’）时，才给予满分；仅回复‘谢谢告知’而无后续澄清动作的，应在‘交互有效性’维度扣分，因为其未能解决沟通中的实际障碍。
